message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS. In GCP the service is called **Compute Engine**.*  
> *The RTX A6000 GPU is available as the `nvidia-a6000` accelerator type.*  
> *You must have the Compute Engine API enabled, the NVIDIA GPU driver installed on the instance, and the appropriate quota for GPUs in your project.*

---

## 1.  `gcloud` CLI command

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Optional script that installs the NVIDIA driver after boot |
| `--scopes` | Gives the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for driver install) |
| `--tags` | Opens ports 80/443 if you want a web server |

#### Example `startup.sh` (install NVIDIA driver)

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
sudo reboot
```

> Save this script as `startup.sh` in the same directory where you run the `gcloud` command.

---

## 2.  REST API call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the raw Compute Engine REST API, send a `POST` request to:

```
https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your values.

### Request body

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to send the request

1. **Authenticate** – obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`.
2. **POST** the JSON body to the URL above with the header `Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>` and `Content-Type: application/json`.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | GPU quota for `nvidia-a6000` in your region |
| ✅ | `gcloud` SDK installed (or use REST) |
| ✅ | `startup.sh` (or metadata script) to install NVIDIA driver |
| ✅ | Proper IAM permissions (e.g., `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`) |

Once the instance is running, SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed. Happy computing!
